## Simple explanation

Latency is how long someone waits for an operation to finish. For an AI
application, it can mean the time from submitting a prompt to receiving a
response, or the time to produce a particular token or prediction.

## Technical explanation

Latency is a time measurement, typically reported in milliseconds or seconds.
The exact start and end points matter: an API's end-to-end latency may include
network travel, queueing, preprocessing, model computation, and response
transfer. Percentiles such as p50 and p95 describe the median and slower
tail of observed requests.

For token-generating models, time to first token and the time between
subsequent tokens are useful separate measures. A system can begin responding
quickly yet take a long time to finish a lengthy answer.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Latency affects user experience, system capacity, and operational cost.
Engineers use consistent latency metrics to compare deployments, set service
objectives, and identify bottlenecks without hiding slow requests behind an
average.

## How it works

Instrument requests with timestamps at meaningful boundaries, then aggregate
the elapsed times over a representative workload. A simplified end-to-end
measurement is:

$$
\text{latency} = t_{\text{response}} - t_{\text{request}}
$$

Measure under realistic concurrency and input sizes. Caching, batching,
hardware, model size, queueing, and network conditions can all change the
result, sometimes in opposing ways.

## Practical example

An assistant may have a p50 response latency of 1.2 seconds but a p95 of 6
seconds. The median experience is quick, while a notable fraction of users
experience delays. The tail may point to queueing or unusually long prompts.

## Common misconceptions

- Average latency alone does not describe the slowest requests users experience.
- Latency is not the same as throughput; a system can serve many requests per second while individual requests remain slow.
- A model's compute time is only one part of end-to-end application latency.
